claimLedger.wording: The documented workflow scans known caches/logs/temp paths, allows preview/exclusion, and confirms deletion. Default items go to Trash; the Trash category empties it permanently, and manual categories show guides only.
claimLedger.excerpt: By default, items go to Trash; only the Trash category empties it permanently. Manual categories show guides only. Lets you preview items and exclude what you want to keep.
claimLedger.conditions: Do not convert this summary to all methods reversible. README also lists builtin cleanup methods; no cleanup performed.

claimLedger.wording: Risky targets start unselected and their items excluded; the documented labels distinguish rebuildable data, re-download/re-login costs, possible user data and manual guidance.
claimLedger.excerpt: Risky categories are unselected by default; even when selected, items are auto-excluded. (Include them in Preview to delete.)
claimLedger.conditions: Safe is a vendor category label, not our safety guarantee.

claimLedger.wording: The README documents target selection and a CLI dry-run report separately from executing cleanup.
claimLedger.conditions: No commands run; copied example output and Freed (dry-run) numbers are not our measurements. A runnable tutorial needs separate safe reproduction.

claimLedger.wording: Homebrew or release-archive installation is documented; Full Disk Access is described as optional but needed for Trash/restricted locations. The build sets MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0 and source declares Go 1.25.0.
claimLedger.excerpt: Optional: Full Disk Access (needed for Trash/restricted locations); MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0; go 1.25.0
claimLedger.conditions: Do not equate build target with independently verified macOS minimum, or source Go version with a binary runtime prerequisite. No settings changed.

claimLedger.wording: The documented scope excludes system optimization and an uninstaller, and lists Homebrew, Docker and old-download scanning. Its target counts are explicitly as of v1.3.6, not a verified v1.6.0 count.

workflow.title: Review terminal cleanup targets before deleting Mac caches
workflow.primaryIntent: Understand a target category versus an approved item in mac-cleanup-go, and distinguish a dry-run report from deletion and free-space change.
workflow.description: Use the documented terminal review workflow to distinguish cache categories, excluded items and confirmation before deciding what to remove. This is a documentation-led guide, not a cleanup test.
outline: After lead: earlier official terminal list with honest version caption
Selection is not permission: risky defaults and per-item exclusions
Dry-run output is a proposal, not recovered space
Trash, built-in methods and manual-only guides have different consequences
Check rebuilding/re-download costs and original files before any approval
When a category cleaner fits, and when storage/activity investigation is the actual job; show labeled Breathing Room preview
workflow.interactionPass: Hand off a non-executing decision checklist: recognize target -> identify method -> review exclusions -> estimate rebuild/download cost -> back up originals -> decide. No filesystem access, live scan, execution button or fake savings counter.
workflow.tutorialBoundary: No untested runnable tutorial or copied sample output presented as our result. No installation/cleanup performed.
